title: Grateful Dead Live at Providence Civic Center on 1973-09-15

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a jazzy 1973 second set loaded with horn‑driven jams like Let It Grow, Eyes of the World and a killer Keith solo.
ai_review.review: The SBD tape delivers the clear, balanced sound typical of 1973 board recordings, letting listeners hear every nuance of the horn section and the band’s improvisational fire.  Highlights include a soaring Let Me Sing Your Blues Away with a standout Keith Godchaux solo, an epic Eyes of the World jam, and a wild Let It Grow that many fans rank among ’73’s best jazz‑infused moments.  While a few reviewers dislike the horns, the overall performance is celebrated as one of the band’s most adventurous shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (4‑5) and strong praise for both musical performance and soundboard quality; weighted average yields ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, balanced mix typical of 1973 board tapes; reviewers note no drop‑outs or muffiness and praise the overall sound.

standout_songs: Let Me Sing Your Blues Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first half stays mellow, then erupts into free‑form jazz after Truckin', with horn‑driven extensions on Eyes of the World and Let It Grow creating a soaring second set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as ‘blow me away’; guitar tone praised as perfect by several reviewers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux delivers a killer solo on Let Me Sing Your Blues Away and is highlighted throughout the jazzy jams.
